name: ct_ap_lymphoma_aspergillosis
scan_type: CT AP with IV contrast portal venous phase
clinical_history:
58M high grade B cell lymphoma, received rituximab and 50% of CHOP therapy, due second cycle of chemotherapy but has ongoing aspergillosis so holding for now
Bone marrow function appears to have improved since first cycle of chemotherapy
However still critically unwell with enterococcus faecium + coagulase neg staph in blood cultures, aspergillosis on sputum culture - receiving meropenem + ambisome + voriconazole + vanc for this as well as prophylactic co-trimozaxole and aciclovir

Haematology have requested for repeat CT AP with contrast for re-staging of lymphoma
findings:
NG tube in situ.
A lot of peripancreatic fluid - extending into lesser sac causing some compression on the greater curvature of stomach - also mass effect on distal CBD causing upstream congestion (max diameter of CBD - 12mm) with mild intrahepatic biliary radical dilatation. Pancreas itself doesn't look engorged, necrosed etc. Moderate background free abdominopelvic fluid too.
Multiple distal ileal loops show mural oedema with some free fluid tracking along the mesenteric roots.
Caecal pole also looks oedematous, largely compressed due to surrounding free fluid in right paracolic gutter.
Gross soft tisue oedema / anasarca also noted.
stable splenomegaly with multifocal patchy/irregular hypodensities like in keeping with mixed infiltration/infarction.
Improved aeration of left lung base but increase right basal segmental collapse/atelectasis
New cavitating lung lesion (15 mm diameter) anterior aspect of right middle lobe, abutting pleura, with internal soft tissue density, crescentic shape, suspicious with aspergilloma.

most of oedema/free fluid is likely being driven by intense systemic inflammatory repsonse / hypoalbunimaema. Pancreatitis lower down on differential, cannot be defiitively ruled  out - needs clinical correlation

name: ct_head_cerebellar_haemorrhage
clinical_history:
onset at 13:30 with left facial droop, left arm and leg weakness and slurred speech.
BP 255/161
findings:
- There is a large area of parenchymal hemorrhage in the right cerebellum measuring 5 cm in diameter with significant peri-lesional vasogenic edema and this is causing major midline shift across the horizontal cerebellar axis with complete effacement of the cerebral aqueduct and fourth ventricle and crowding of the foramen magnum due to ipsilateral tonsillar herniation

- There is some regional subarachnoid and subdural extension of haemorrhage along the tentorium

- The background brain parenchyma otherwise appears unremarkable with no gross areas of infarction

- Background chronic small vessel ischemic changes and age-appropriate involutional atrophy are noted with asymmetric predominance of the right frontal lobe

name: ct_tap_acute_abdomen_gda_bleed
clinical_history: 72F, admitted 4 days ago with confusion and falls. Background AF on apixaban, T2DM, previous right MCA stroke with residual left hemiparesis. Today developed acute abdominal pain localised to epigastrium with associated vomiting. Lactate 4.2, Hb dropped from 112 to 87 over 24 hours. Query mesenteric ischaemia, query GI bleed source, query intra-abdominal pathology. Previous imaging includes CT head on admission (old infarct only) and an abdominal ultrasound 6 months ago (fatty liver, small abdominal aortic aneurysm 3.8cm infrarenal).
findings:
Scan performed thorax abdomen pelvis portal venous phase, no arterial phase obtained
Large volume haemoperitoneum throughout abdomen and pelvis, highest density in pelvis and around liver
Active contrast extravasation from gastroduodenal artery branch, approximately 2cm distal to origin, forming a small pseudoaneurysm approximately 8mm
Duodenum D1/D2 shows wall thickening and mural gas, adjacent fat stranding
Infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm now measures 4.6cm, previously 3.8cm on US 6 months ago, no evidence of rupture or contained leak
Pancreas appears atrophic with pancreatic duct dilation to 6mm, calcifications within pancreatic head, consistent with chronic pancreatitis
Multiple small hypodensities in both kidneys, largest 1.2cm right interpolar, not fully characterised on this phase
Large hiatus hernia with approximately 40% of stomach intrathoracic
Bilateral dependent atelectasis, small right pleural effusion
Left adrenal thickening, nodular, 2.4cm, not previously characterised
Cholelithiasis, no wall thickening
Moderate bilateral pelvic free fluid continuous with the haemoperitoneum
Old right MCA territory encephalomalacia visible on scout images only
Bladder partially distended, catheter not yet placed
Diffuse colonic faecal loading
Background mild-moderate atherosclerosis

name: ct_ap_cholecystitis_descriptor_stress
clinical_history: 52F with right upper quadrant pain, fever 38.9, WCC 18
findings: The gallbladder is distended measuring 11 cm in long axis with marked wall thickening to 6 mm. Pericholecystic fluid and fat stranding are present. A 15 mm calculus is impacted in the cystic duct neck. Gallbladder wall hyperenhancement is noted. No pneumobilia or portal venous gas. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation; CBD measures 5 mm. Liver is normal in size and attenuation with no focal lesion. Pancreas, spleen, kidneys, and adrenals are unremarkable. Bowel loops are normal in calibre without wall thickening or obstruction. No free intraperitoneal fluid or air. Bladder and uterus and ovaries are unremarkable. No pelvic or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. No acute osseous abnormality. Lung bases are clear.

name: ct_thorax_pleural_tethering_stress
clinical_history: 65M smoker, incidental pulmonary nodule on recent chest X-ray, for characterisation
findings: A 28 mm spiculated mass in the left upper lobe apicoposterior segment. The mass abuts the parietal pleura without frank invasion. It tethers the adjacent visceral pleura with surface retraction but no discrete pleural nodularity. The fat plane between the mass and the aortic arch is preserved. The mass is closely apposed to but does not encase the left upper lobe bronchus; bronchial patency is maintained. No cavitation. Left hilar node measures 11 mm in short axis. No mediastinal lymphadenopathy. No pleural effusion. No contralateral pulmonary nodules. No adrenal or hepatic metastases within the imaged upper abdomen. Background upper lobe centrilobular emphysema. No bony lesion.

No free intraperitoneal air or fluid. No lymphadenopathy. No acute osseous lesion. The lung bases are clear.
